chunks: The birth pangs led her to the trunk of a date-palm tree. She said, 'Would that I had died before this and become a thing forgotten, unremembered.'

key_terms.جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ: The trunk of the date palm tree
key_terms.يَا لَيْتَنِي: Would that I were / I wish

ai.seo_question: What did Maryam say when she gave birth under the date palm tree?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse captures Maryam’s moment of profound human vulnerability and solitude (khalwa) before the divine intervention, illustrating the transition from natural instinct to spiritual fortitude. Scholars note that her wish for oblivion reflects the societal stigma of her time, making the subsequent miracle of the palm tree and the infant’s speech a direct counter to her isolation. This event underscores the concept of 'Ismah' (infallibility/protection) not as absence of feeling, but as divine support during trials.
